item.title: Xavi satisfied as Gakpo earns Oranje late draw against Germany
item.description:
Xavi satisfied as Gakpo earns Oranje late draw against Germany

September 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

New Dutch national football coach Xavi Hernandez declared himself satisfied with his team’s performance following the 1-1 draw with Germany in Amsterdam.

Cody Gakpo converted a magnificent skewered pass by debutant Ruben van Bommel with a crashing volley in stoppage time to earn Oranje the point their second-half dominance deserved.

“We were a little nervous in the first half, but the second half is the way we want to play,” the Spaniard said after the opening game in the Nations League, his first match since being appointed last month.

Germany took the lead in the 32nd minute when Felix Nmecha pounced on a loose ball in the penalty, but the Dutch were aggrieved that their opponents had played on after Brian Brobbey went down injured in the centre circle.

Captain Virgil van Dijk said: “We thought the ball should have gone out, but it didn’t go out, and it was unfortunate that it fell right in front of them after a good block by Jan Paul van Hecke.”

Van Dijk had the ball in the net after 15 minutes, but his header was disallowed after the referee decided Brobbey had impeded goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen.

New striker needed

Brobbey was replaced by AZ striker Mexx Meerdink, who missed a glorious chance to equalise on his debut after Crysencio Summerville made space in the penalty area with a smart turn.

Xavi said afterwards he would look at calling up a replacement striker ahead of Sunday’s match against Serbia in Belgrade, but did not comment on who it might be. Wout Weghorst could be recalled after being left out of the squad initially, while other contenders include Zian Flemming of Ipswich and FC Köln’s Thijs Dallinga.

Van Bommel, who became the third generation of his family to play for Oranje after and his father, Mark, his grandfather, Bert van Marwijk, came on in the second half and capped his debut with the assist that set up Gakpo’s goal.

“I ran forward and I saw Cody free at the far post, and I thought, I have to get it to him somehow. It wasn’t an easy finish, but the pass wasn’t bad either,” the PSV winger said.

Another second-half substitute was Borussia Dortmund midfielder Joey Veerman, who made his first appearance in an orange shirt for two years after being frozen out of the international set-up by Xavi’s predecessor Ronald Koeman. Veerman came on for Marseille’s Quinten Timber, who was selected to take the place of the injured Frenkie de Jong.

item.title: Dutch PM Jetten warns “hands off the ICC” in debut UN speech
item.description:
Dutch PM Jetten warns “hands off the ICC” in debut UN speech

September 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Prime minister Rob Jetten gave a fiery address to the United Nations on Thursday, defending the International Criminal Court and the rule of law.

“Hands off the ICC and all those other institutions that protect the international legal order,” he said in his first address at the UN’s annual meeting in New York.

Although Jetten did not call out American president Donald Trump specifically, the speech came after reporting earlier this week that the United States is planning to escalate its fight with the ICC and sanction the institution as a whole as part of its campaign to dismantle the court “brick by brick”.

The White House has already sanctioned 13 staff members, including court president, Japanese Judge Tomoko Akane, over the investigation into alleged Israeli war crimes in Gaza.

“Take, for example, the attempts to undermine the International Criminal Court – a court based in my country, in my city. This undermines the international legal order as a whole. And that affects us all,” Jetten said.

As the court’s host state, the Netherlands is obliged to provide assistance such as cooperation with security, facilitating visas and transporting defendants and witnesses.

He also called for Russia to be held accountable for the war in Ukraine. “In this conflict, Ukraine has no choice but to defend itself,” said Jetten. “But Russia chooses to wage war day after day,” he said.

item.title: Van Weel survives no-confidence debate over crime stats row
item.description:
Van Weel survives no-confidence debate over crime stats row

September 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Justice minister David van Weel has survived a motion of no confidence after he apologised to MPs who accused him of misleading them over police crime figures.

MPs called an emergency debate on Thursday over the minister’s response to reports that police had not responded to some 10,000 criminal complaints because they lacked the capacity to do so.

Van Weel told parliament in June that more than half the cases were reports of crimes rather than official complaints, which police are required to investigate.

But he was corrected by the government’s audit office, the Algemene Rekenkamer, which said in its annual report to parliament that only 10% of the cited cases were verbal reports.

“The consequence is that victims of crimes such as sexual offences and serious theft had not had justice and these serious cases have not had any significant attention,” the auditors wrote.

Van Weel initially tried to shrug off the reprimand as a “difference of insight”, but after MPs called a debate and tabled a motion of no confidence he attempted to apologise for his choice of words.

Measures of crime

The minister blamed the confusion on the different criteria used to measure the seriousness of the complaint. Police prioritise crimes based on how much evidence is available to start an investigation, such as witness statements and camera footage, while auditors use the “Crime Harm Index”, which looks at the severity of sentences imposed by courts.

Van Weel acknowledged that he had “given the impression” that he “had trivialised the seriousness of the Court of Audit’s report”, but insisted: “That doesn’t make it wrong information.

Opposition MPs said the minister’s explanation did not go far enough and threatened to back a motion of no confidence tabled by the far-right PVV, which would have forced Van Weel to resign.

Different attitude

“The minister has had several chances to say he gave parliament the wrong impression, but hasn’t taken them,” said Caroline van der Plas of the farmers’ party BBB.

Van Weel made a second, stronger apology that stopped short of admitting he had misled MPs, which was enough to persuade all parties not to vote for the motion, with the exception of the PVV and Forum voor Democratie.

“I realise now, after your contributions, that I intentionally or unintentionally gave you the wrong impression and that you felt misled,” he said. “That was never my intention, but it shouldn’t have happened.”

“At the last minute we saw a different attitude,” Ingrid Coenradie of right-wing opposition party JA21 commented. “We would have liked to have seen that at the start.”

item.title: Seven arrests at protest against refugee facility in Gelderland
item.description:
Seven arrests at protest against refugee facility in Gelderland

September 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police have broken up a protest in Gelderland against a planned asylum seekers’ centre after fireworks were thrown from the crowd.

Seven people were arrested as the demonstration outside the village hall in Kesteren threatened to turn violent at around 9pm. Police cleared the area by 11pm, taking some demonstrators away in vans.

Some 300 people responded to a call on social media to gather outside the building on Thursday after the local council banned demonstrations in the neighbouring village of Opleusden, where riots broke out a week ago.

Neder-Betuwe councillors were meeting in Opleusden to discuss plans to accommodate 132 refugees, including eight unaccompanied minors, in a former transformer station.

The meeting was moved forward from 8pm to 6pm and lasted just 17 minutes after all political parties agreed in advance to approve the plan, mayor Jan Kottelenberg said.

The area outside the town hall was subjected to an emergency order banning public gatherings after last week’s riots outside the previous council meeting, which led to 14 arrests.

Towns and villages across the Netherlands have been the scene of violent protests against asylum seekers’ centres across the Netherlands, often organised by far-right “Defend” groups.

A group calling itself We Are The People called an anti-asylum march in The Hague at the weekend that was cancelled by the mayor when participants chanted racist slogans, threw fireworks and traffic poles at police and refused to remove face masks.

item.title: Fifth West Nile virus death confirmed as number of cases rises
item.description:
Fifth West Nile virus death confirmed as number of cases rises

September 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A fifth person has died after contracting the West Nile virus since the turn of the year, while the number of confirmed infections has increased to 44.

The public health agency RIVM said another 16 patients had been detected since the last update a week ago. The agency has stressed there is no risk of a pandemic because the virus cannot be transmitted from person to person.

Doctors, vets, virologists and other specialists are monitoring the spread of the disease and deciding if extra precautionary measures need to be taken.

The virus, which is transmitted by mosquitos, causes no symptoms in 80% of people who contract it. but West Nile fever leads to neurological problems in around 1% of cases and in exceptional cases it can be fatal.

Following the death of a hospital patient in Utrecht, the RIVM said last month that the virus was now circulating in the Dutch mosquito population. Previous deaths had been limited to people who were infected while travelling abroad.

Around half the infections reported to the RIVM this year have been in Zuid-Holland province, with other cases in Utrecht, Noord-Holland and Noord-Brabant, Gelderland and Overijssel.

West Nile virus can also be contracted by other species such as birds and horses, but they cannot transmit the infection to humans. The RIVM has recorded 136 positive tests in horses and 171 in birds so far this year.

item.title: Meta takes down Dutch satirist’s film made with Meta glasses
item.description:
Meta takes down Dutch satirist’s film made with Meta glasses

September 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Instagram removed a video by Roel Maalderink in which the satirical journalist films himself asking the employees of parent company Meta how they feel about the controversial camera glasses.

In the short video, which can still be seen on Alphabet-owned YouTube, Maalderink dons the so-called “pervert glasses” and quizzes staff after instructing the device to start recording.

The gadgets, the most popular version of which is sold by Meta, look like normal glasses but allow users to film and take photos covertly.

The employees, all of whom have their features blurred and are unrecognisable, are not pleased about being recorded.

The video, made together with digital rights organisation Bits of Freedom, was removed from Instagram over what Meta said was “bullying and harassment”.

“I’ve been making satirical videos about everything for 10 years now: Gaza, Ukraine, refugees,” Maalderink said in a statement. He added that this was the first time he had had a video taken down.

Bits of Freedom said that this behaviour shows the company’s power. “Meta determines what becomes publicly discussable and how the debate unfolds. Apparently, there’s no room for criticism directed at Meta itself,” the organisation said.

Earlier this week, Dutch privacy watchdog AP warned that sharing images made with camera glasses violates GDPR rules unless permission is given by everyone in the image.

item.title: Ships on IJssel restricted to one-way traffic as drought lingers
item.description:
Ships on IJssel restricted to one-way traffic as drought lingers

September 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Highways agency Rijkswaterstaat has imposed a one-way system on the IJssel river in the east of the country because of falling river levels.

From Friday morning barges and boats travelling from Arnhem to Zutphen will have to take a detour of up to 300km.

Rijkswaterstaat said the water channel in the river was too shallow to allow ships to pass each other.

The summer drought has brought the flow in the major Dutch rivers down to unprecedented levels, with the Rhine down to 600 cubic metres a second at Lobith, the point where it enters the Netherlands from Germany.

Koninklijke Binnnenvaart Nederland, which represents inland waterway users, said it was a further blow for a sector that had already been forced to adopt limits on its activities.

Spokesman Andries de Weerd told NOS: “We’ve been taking half or even one-third loads, and now we’re having take the long route round, so unfortunately the costs are going to go up a little.”

item.title: No trains to Amsterdam central station next weekend
item.description:
No trains to Amsterdam central station next weekend

September 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Railtrack operator ProRail has announced there will be no trains to or from Amsterdam central station on Saturday, October 3 due to maintenance works.

The timetable on Sunday, October 4 and Monday, October 5 will also be significantly altered. International trains to and from Germany will terminate at Utrecht.

The work is part of ongoing renovations at the capital’s main train station. Currently it services around 200,000 travelers per day, one of the busiest in the country. That number is expected to grow to 275,000 per day.

Platforms are being widened and staircases are being added to accommodate the increase.

ProRail advises anyone traveling to Amsterdam to check the NS travel planner.

item.title: Repairs to A15 motorway bridge will cost hauliers €600k a day
item.description:
Repairs to A15 motorway bridge will cost hauliers €600k a day

September 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The partial closure of a motorway bridge in Rotterdam for repairs is expected to cost the transport sector at least €600,000 a day because of longer journeys.

The bridge, which carries traffic on the A15 to the Maasvlakte, was closed a week ago on safety grounds after inspectors found cracks in the main beam.

Traffic will be restricted to the hard shoulder during emergency repairs, which are expected to last six to eight weeks. The bridge carries 36,500 vehicles a day, including 15,500 heavy goods vehicles.

On the first day of the works, September 17, a 12km tailback built up behind the bridge, adding an hour to the journey.

Transport en Logistiek Nederland (TLN), which represents the sector, surveyed its members on the impact of the closure and found that they expect journeys to take an extra 15 to 60 minutes.

Every 30-minute delay costs €600,000 when projected across an entire day’s traffic, TLN calculated.

“The longer the disruption lasts, the faster the damage adds up,” said TLN chair Elisabeth Post. “Especially if the old bridge eventually has to be removed entirely, which will reduce capacity further.”

The road and rail bridges were last renovated in 2021, ahead of plans to replace them entirely after 2030.

The state of infrastructure in the Netherlands is becoming a growing problem. The Merwedebrug, which takes traffic on the A27, was closed to lorries and coaches in July, at a cost of €1.5 million a day, while the A28 at Nijkerk was shut for 48 hours at the start of September after inspectors found sand and gravel holding up the base supports had been eroded.

The government announced an extra investment of €1.5 billion in next year’s budget to spend on maintaining roads, railways and waterways, but the full cost of the maintenance backlog is estimate to run into the tens of millions.

item.title: Gelderland to impose nitrogen limits on farms despite BBB split
item.description:
Gelderland to impose nitrogen limits on farms despite BBB split

September 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Gelderland has become the first province to restrict farming in “buffer zones” around nature reserves to bring down nitrogen compound emissions.

The provincial assembly voted to draw a 500-metre cordon around the Veluwe and three other vulnerable areas, in anticipation of nationwide restrictions that the government is drawing up.

New livestock farms and extensions to existing ones will be banned within the buffer zones from this year.

Other limitations will be phased in over the next 10 years, including a ban on synthetic fertiliser, restrictions on gas consumption and an obligation to make cattle sheds more energy efficient.

The plans have divided the parties in the agricultural province, which has the highest levels of ammonia pollution in the Netherlands.

They were drawn up by Ans Mol, executive member for the farmers’ party BBB, who said that doing nothing would mean “very big risks” for the sector. But seven of the BBB’s 12 assembly members voted against the plan.

Farmers’ protests

Coalition partners VVD, CDA, ChristenUnie and the SGP all backed the measures, which were also supported by the opposition parties GroenLinks, PvdA and D66.

Farmers picketed the provincial assembly building in Arnhem at the weekend to protest against nitrogen restrictions, arguing that they were not supported by evidence and deprived farmers of a future.

The provincial plans have been announced while the government in The Hague is still drawing up its own schedule of measures to bring down nitrogen pollution so that major housebuilding and infrastructure projects can go ahead.

Chris Backes, professor of environmental law at Utrecht University, has warned that some provinces will have to bring in their own measures to prevent the government using the “emergency brake” of a 5% to 10% reduction in heads of cattle.

Farmers are also facing legal action from environmental campaign groups such as Mobilisation for the Environment (MOB), which has petitioned regional courts to cancel the licences for 130 farm businesses.

All construction projects have to obtain a nature permit which shows they comply with environmental regulations, including European limits on nitrogen compound emissions around Natura-2000 conservation areas.
